newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka to stop enquiring about investment sources.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka to stop enquiring about investment sources.

text.p: Bangladesh, anxious to increase investment, will stop requiring local businessmen to declare the source of money they invest in the country, the finance minister said.
"The government will no longer enquire about the source of money invested," S.A.M.S. Kibria said on Saturday.
"A government notification in this regard will be published soon," Kibria was quoted by newspapers as telling a business seminar in the northeastern district of Sylhet.
The minister also said a decision would soon be made to free industrial investment from tax. He did not elaborate.
Investors in Bangladesh are currently bound by law to declare the source of investment funds to revenue authorities.
Bangladesh's Board of Investment (BOI) last month recommended the Finance Ministry remove the law to encourage investment.

"The binding shies away many black money holders who could otherwise be potential investors. There is no denying that many in Bangladesh have black money which is either pushing up inflation or being flighted abroad," a senior BOI official told Reuters on Sunday.
Bangladesh officials use the term black money to refer to income that is not declared to the tax authorities or which may have been earned through illegal activities such as smuggling.
The government has also said it is keen to attract foreign investment.

Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed said last month the government expected $2 bilion in foreign direct investment in fiscal 1996-97 (July-June) compared with less than $250 million over past five years.
